---
title: "ADS-C in the OPDI trajectory"
subtitle: "Version 1 — what a satellite cruise feed adds to flight-event extraction"
author: "EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit — Open Performance Data Initiative"
date: last-modified
abstract: |
  OPDI builds every track from ADS-B state vectors. OpenSky also publishes an
  ADS-C feed, and the obvious hypothesis is that merging the two improves
  coverage and therefore milestone extraction. This paper tests it. ADS-C is
  merged into the state-vector frame *before* segmentation, so `track_id` sees
  both sources; the trajectory cleaner is made source-aware, because its
  twenty-second isolated-point rule would otherwise delete a feed whose median
  cadence is ten minutes. Both arms — ADS-B only, and ADS-B plus ADS-C — are
  rebuilt from the same state vectors with the same segmentation and the same
  detectors, and scored against EUROCONTROL APDF over the twenty aerodromes
  and three days of flight events version 4.

  The feed is narrow and the result is correspondingly narrow. Measured over
  eleven days spanning 2023-09 to 2026-10, ADS-C delivers a few thousand rows
  a day inside OPDI's European box at a median of several hundred seconds
  between reports; almost all of those rows are above FL300 and most sit west
  of 10°W. It carries no `on_ground` flag and almost nothing below ten thousand
  feet. The A-CDM runway family therefore cannot move, and this paper reports
  that as a measured null rather than omitting it.

  The two feeds also do not share a clock, and neither states a position age
  that can be used. Comparing ADS-C reports against ADS-B interpolated to the
  same instant separates the two candidate explanations: the feeds agree about
  where the track is to within a few metres across track while disagreeing by
  hundreds of metres along it, which is a timing offset and not a position
  error. That offset is a property of the individual airframe rather than of
  the feed, so no global correction is applied and the paper says why.

  Every figure is produced by `benchmarks/regenerate_adsc_v1.py`. Where an
  output is not staged the table says so in place rather than being omitted.
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrreprt
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
---

```{r regenerate}
#| include: false
#| cache: false

# Rendering this page runs the analysis behind it.
#
# `regenerate_adsc_v1.py` is the executable definition of the study: each CSV
# read below is produced by exactly one job it declares, with exactly the
# arguments it declares. It re-runs a job when the *code that job depends on*
# has changed since the output was written -- not when the file is old, which
# says nothing. A render with everything current is a fast no-op; a render
# after editing `osn_adsc.py`, `tracks.py` or `cleaning/native.py` re-runs the
# pipeline jobs before the first table is drawn.
#
# OPDI_RENDER selects what happens instead:
#
#   run          (default) regenerate anything stale, then render
#   check        fail fast naming every stale job, regenerate nothing
#   allow-stale  render a draft from whatever is staged, after naming staleness
#   skip         do not invoke the entrypoint at all
#
# One thing the entrypoint cannot regenerate: the two pipeline arms at
# s3a://eurocontrol/opdi/research/adsc/{base,merged}, built by
# benchmarks/run_adsc_day.py at roughly six cluster-hours for three days. The
# jobs read those tables; if they have not been built, the jobs fail rather
# than reporting a zero. See [Reproducing this].
REPO   <- Sys.getenv("OPDI_REPO_DIR",
                     normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), "..", "..", "..", "opdi"),
                                   mustWork = FALSE))
PYTHON <- Sys.getenv("OPDI_PYTHON", file.path(REPO, ".venv310", "bin", "python"))
MODE   <- Sys.getenv("OPDI_RENDER", "run")

regen <- file.path(REPO, "benchmarks", "regenerate_adsc_v1.py")
if (!file.exists(regen) && MODE != "skip") {
  stop("regenerate_adsc_v1.py not found under REPO=", REPO,
       " -- set OPDI_REPO_DIR, or OPDI_RENDER=skip to render without it.")
}

if (MODE != "skip" && file.exists(regen)) {
  flags <- switch(MODE,
                  "run" = character(0),
                  "check" = "--check",
                  "allow-stale" = c("--check", "--allow-stale"),
                  character(0))
  status <- system2(PYTHON, c(shQuote(regen), flags), stdout = "", stderr = "")
  if (!identical(status, 0L)) {
    stop("regenerate_adsc_v1.py exited ", status,
         " -- the figures below would not match the code that is checked out. ",
         "Set OPDI_RENDER=allow-stale to render anyway.")
  }
}
```

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(knitr)

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

# Read-only. Every figure and table on this page comes from a committed CSV.
# Nothing here reads S3, a database or a Spark cluster.
D <- function(f) {
  p <- file.path("data", f)
  if (!file.exists(p)) return(NULL)
  read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

census <- D("adsc_census.csv")                      # one row per sampled day
gain   <- D("adsc_gain_2026.csv")                   # one row per arm + extension
holes  <- D("adsc_holes_2026.csv")                  # one row per bridged hole
sync   <- D("adsc_time_sync_2026.csv")              # one row per airframe + ALL
syncp  <- D("adsc_time_sync_pairs_2026.csv")        # one row per bracketed pair
ev     <- D("adsc_events_2026.csv")                 # one row per (arm, milestone)
evap   <- D("adsc_events_by_airport_2026.csv")      # + per aerodrome

# A missing file is reported in place, never silently skipped: a chapter whose
# table vanished reads as a chapter with nothing to say.
missing_note <- function(name) {
  sprintf(paste("*`%s` is not staged, so this section's figures are absent",
                "rather than wrong. Run `python",
                "benchmarks/regenerate_adsc_v1.py` with cluster credentials;",
                "the [Provenance] chapter lists what is present.*"), name)
}

# One accessor per file. Each returns a visible placeholder when the file is
# absent -- a draft with holes is honest -- and **stops** when the file is
# present but the row is not. Those are different failures: the first is work
# not yet done, the second is a table that disagrees with itself, and only the
# second may not be rendered.
ABSENT <- "(not staged)"

acc <- function(frame, label) {
  function(where, col) {
    if (is.null(frame)) return(ABSENT)
    v <- frame[where(frame), col]
    if (length(v) != 1) stop("no single ", label, " row for ", col)
    v
  }
}

GAIN_ <- acc(gain, "gain")
GAIN  <- function(arm, col) GAIN_(function(d) d$arm == arm, col)
SYNC_ <- acc(sync, "time-sync")
SYNC  <- function(icao24, col) SYNC_(function(d) d$icao24 == icao24, col)
CEN_  <- acc(census, "census")
CEN   <- function(day, col) CEN_(function(d) d$day == day, col)

# Formatters that survive the placeholder: a draft must not fail on sprintf.
fmt <- function(f) function(x) if (identical(x, ABSENT)) ABSENT else sprintf(f, x)
num    <- function(x) if (identical(x, ABSENT)) ABSENT else
  formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
p1     <- fmt("%.1f")
p2     <- fmt("%.2f")
signed <- fmt("%+.2f")
pct    <- fmt("%.1f%%")

rng <- function(col, digits = 0) {
  if (is.null(census)) return(ABSENT)
  v <- census[[col]]
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f-%.", digits, "f"), min(v), max(v))
}
study_rng <- function(col, digits = 0) {
  if (is.null(census)) return(ABSENT)
  v <- census[census$day %in% STUDY_DAYS, col]
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f-%.", digits, "f"), min(v), max(v))
}

# Configuration, not measurement. Named here so the prose and the parameter
# table read one source -- `AdscConfig` and `CleaningConfig` in
# `src/opdi/config.py`, and `adsc_time_sync.py`'s default.
SHADOW_BEFORE_S <- 60
SHADOW_AFTER_S  <- 60
TIME_OFFSET_S   <- 0.0
HOLE_SECONDS    <- 300
ISOLATED_GAP_S  <- 20
MAX_GAP_S       <- 60
STUDY_DAYS      <- c("2026-06-05", "2026-06-06", "2026-06-07")
```

# What the feed is

OpenSky publishes an ADS-C topic beside the ADS-B archive:
`s3a://readsb-aircraft-states/topics/readsb.aircraft.adsc.avro`, hourly
partitions named `hour=<unix seconds>`, holding snappy **parquet** despite the
`.avro` in the topic name — the files carry the Avro schema
`org.opensky.avro.readsb.Aircraft` in their footer. Partitions run from
2023-07-07 to the current hour, 982 days with 24 gaps longer than a day, and
in 2026 the feed averages 22.3 of 24 hourly partitions per day. A missing hour
is routine, and the ingest tolerates it by listing before reading rather than
letting `spark.read.parquet` raise `PATH_NOT_FOUND` on the first absent one.

```{r census-table}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(census)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_census.csv"))
} else {
  cols <- c("day", "hour_partitions", "rows", "rows_in_box",
            "airframes_in_box", "median_cadence_s", "in_box_above_fl300",
            "in_box_below_10000ft", "in_box_west_of_10w", "in_box_on_ground",
            "exact_duplicate_rows")
  kable(census[, cols], row.names = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Day", "Hours read", "Rows", "In box",
                      "Airframes in box", "Median cadence (s)", "> FL300",
                      "< 10,000 ft", "West of 10°W", "On ground",
                      "Exact duplicates"),
        caption = paste("The raw ADS-C topic, by sampled day. Every band after",
                        "`In box` is counted **inside** OPDI's published",
                        "European coverage box -- that is the population the",
                        "pipeline would ingest. `Hours read` matters: a day",
                        "with 6 of 24 partitions present has a cadence that",
                        "reflects the gap, not the feed."))
}
```

Reading that table across the archive: the feed delivers `r rng("rows")` rows a
day worldwide and `r rng("rows_in_box")` inside the coverage box, from
`r rng("airframes_in_box")` in-box airframes. On the three study days it is
`r study_rng("rows_in_box")` in-box rows from `r study_rng("airframes_in_box")`
airframes, at a median of `r study_rng("median_cadence_s", 0)` seconds between
reports from one aircraft. **Against the 5 s resolution OPDI ingests ADS-B at,
that is a feed roughly two orders of magnitude sparser.**

It is also a *cruise* feed, and that is what bounds what it can contribute.
Of the in-box rows, `r if (is.null(census)) ABSENT else sprintf("%.1f-%.1f%%", min(100*census$in_box_above_fl300/census$rows_in_box), max(100*census$in_box_above_fl300/census$rows_in_box))`
are above FL300 and
`r if (is.null(census)) ABSENT else sprintf("%.1f-%.1f%%", min(100*census$in_box_west_of_10w/census$rows_in_box), max(100*census$in_box_west_of_10w/census$rows_in_box))`
sit west of 10°W — the North Atlantic corner of the box. The whole box sees
`r rng("in_box_below_10000ft")` rows a day below ten thousand feet, and
**`on_ground` is true for `r if (is.null(census)) ABSENT else sum(census$in_box_on_ground)` rows across every day sampled.**
There is also no redelivery to clean up: `r if (is.null(census)) ABSENT else sum(census$exact_duplicate_rows)`
exact duplicates in total, so the ingest's deduplication has never had anything
to remove.

```{r census-fill}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(census)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_census.csv"))
} else {
  fill_cols <- grep("^fill_", names(census), value = TRUE)
  worst <- data.frame(
    column = sub("^fill_", "", fill_cols),
    max_fill = sapply(fill_cols, function(c) max(census[[c]], na.rm = TRUE)))
  worst <- worst[order(-worst$max_fill), ]
  kable(worst, row.names = FALSE, digits = 1,
        col.names = c("Column", "Best fill rate on any sampled day (%)"),
        caption = paste("Every column of the feed, by the best fill rate it",
                        "reached on any sampled day. A column at 0.0 here was",
                        "empty on **every** day sampled -- which is the",
                        "evidence for not carrying it into the OPDI schema."))
}
```

That table is the reason this study carries five fields and not twenty-five. A
reader would reasonably expect an ADS-C report to bring indicated airspeed,
Mach, outside air temperature, wind, the selected altitude from the FMS, and
the aircraft's registration and type. The `readsb` record has a column for each
of them, and **every one measured 0.0% on all eleven days**. They are not
discarded by OPDI; they are not there. The same is true of `alt_geom`, so an
ADS-C sample contributes barometric altitude and no geometric altitude at all.
`nic`, `rc`, `seen`, `seen_pos` and `rssi` are present but constant — zero,
zero, zero, zero and −49.5 — which makes them defaults rather than
measurements, and they are not carried as if they were.

```{r census-growth}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(census)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_census.csv"))
} else {
  g <- census[, c("day", "fill_track", "fill_gs", "fill_baro_rate",
                  "fill_flight", "fill_squawk", "fill_on_ground")]
  kable(g, row.names = FALSE, digits = 1,
        col.names = c("Day", "track", "gs", "baro_rate", "flight", "squawk",
                      "on_ground"),
        caption = paste("Fill rate by day for the columns that are sometimes",
                        "populated. The feed's schema has **grown**: two step",
                        "changes, neither announced anywhere."))
}
```

Two step changes are visible there, and neither is documented upstream.
`track`, `gs` and `baro_rate` are empty until somewhere between 2025-03 and
2025-09; `flight`, `squawk` and `on_ground` until between 2026-03 and 2026-06.
Before roughly 2025-09 the feed is position and barometric altitude and nothing
else. For this study that is harmless — the three study days are fully
populated, and the callsign is deliberately dropped in any case — but **a
merged arm over 2023 or 2024 would write ADS-C rows with NULL `velocity` and
NULL `vert_rate`**, and any speed-based detector would see NULL rather than a
value on those rows. If the study period ever moves back, that moves with it.

# How it is merged

| Decision | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Merge point | Before segmentation | `TrackProcessor._merge_adsc` |
| Default | Off (`adsc.enabled = False`) | `AdscConfig` |
| ADS-C callsign | `NULL` | `osn_adsc.to_opdi_schema` |
| Shadow window | −`r SHADOW_BEFORE_S` s … +`r SHADOW_AFTER_S` s | `AdscConfig.shadow_{before,after}_seconds` |
| Global time correction | `r TIME_OFFSET_S` s (off) | `AdscConfig.time_offset_seconds` |
| Thinning applied to ADS-C | None | `AdscIngestion.ingest_from_s3` |
| Isolated-point rule | Exempt for ADS-C | `CleaningConfig.sparse_sources` |
| Stale-broadcast rule | Exempt for ADS-C | `CleaningConfig.sparse_sources` |
| Dedup tie-break | ADS-B wins | `drop_duplicate_statevectors` |
| Derivative-spike filter | Unchanged | `mask_derivative_spikes` |
| Segment split | Unchanged, `r HOLE_SECONDS` s | `CleaningConfig.segment_gap_seconds` |

Four of those need an argument rather than an assertion.

**Why before segmentation.** The hypothesis is about coverage and track
continuity, and both are properties of `track_id` — which `_add_track_id`
assigns from the frame it is handed. Merging afterwards could only attach ADS-C
to tracks ADS-B had already drawn, which answers a different question: *which
ADS-B tracks can ADS-C be attached to*, rather than *what tracks do the two
feeds make together*. A test reads that ordering off the source of
`process_month` so it cannot drift.

**Why the callsign is dropped.** The feed's `flight` field carries the IATA
commercial number — `LH133`, `AF805`, `AY68` — and ADS-B broadcasts the ICAO
callsign, `DLH133`. The production segmentation arm (A9, `debounced`) breaks a
track when the last non-blank callsign changes, so carrying `flight` through
would trip that break at every ADS-C sample and split precisely the tracks the
merge exists to join. A9 bridges NULLs by design, with
`F.last(..., ignorenulls=True)`, so NULL removes a false signal rather than
losing a true one. An IATA-to-ICAO mapping would recover the field; it was not
attempted here.

**Why the cleaner had to change.** `CleaningConfig.isolated_max_gap_seconds` is
`r ISOLATED_GAP_S` s, and `mask_isolated_points` NULLs any value whose nearest
same-column neighbour is further away than that on *both* sides. At a cadence
of several hundred seconds that is every ADS-C sample, in every column it
touches. Left unexempted, step 02a would delete the position, altitude and
speed of the entire feed it had just been handed — and the merged arm would then
score identically to the baseline for a reason having nothing to do with the
hypothesis. A test asserts exactly that failure with the exemption switched
off, so the result cannot be quietly reintroduced.

**Why `track_id` changes, and what that costs.** Enabling the merge is a fourth
`track_id` boundary after legacy → A8 → A9. Like those it is silent to a joiner
— an empty join, not an error — and that is why both arms of this study live
under `s3a://eurocontrol/opdi/research/adsc/` and the flag ships off. No
published table moves.

# Whether the two clocks agree

ADS-B and ADS-C arrive over different links and neither states a position age
that can be used. ADS-B's `last_pos_update` is real but small. ADS-C's `seen`
and `seen_pos` are constant zero — the feed *asserts* that every report is
current — and the `readsb` record does not expose the ADS-C report's own
time-of-position, so there is nothing in band to correct from. The skew was
therefore measured.

For each ADS-C report with an ADS-B sample of the same airframe within
`r MAX_GAP_S` s on **both** sides, the ADS-B position is interpolated to the
ADS-C timestamp and the offset decomposed against the direction the ADS-B pair
actually moved — not against the broadcast heading, which in wind is not where
the aircraft is going. **Cross-track** is what the two feeds disagree about
that no timing explanation can absorb; **along-track divided by ground speed**
is the implied time offset. A position error is isotropic and lands in both; a
timing error lands only along track.

```{r sync-overall}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(sync)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_time_sync_2026.csv"))
} else {
  a <- sync[sync$icao24 == "ALL", ]
  kable(data.frame(
    quantity = c("Bracketed pairs", "Median |cross-track|",
                 "Median |along-track|", "Along:cross ratio",
                 "Median implied offset", "sigma of implied offset"),
    value = c(num(a$n), paste0(p1(a$median_abs_cross_m), " m"),
              paste0(p1(a$median_abs_along_m), " m"),
              paste0(p1(a$median_abs_along_m /
                          max(a$median_abs_cross_m, 1e-9)), "x"),
              paste0(signed(a$median_implied_dt_s), " s"),
              paste0(p1(a$std_implied_dt_s), " s"))),
    row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("", "Measured"),
    caption = paste("ADS-C against interpolated ADS-B over",
                    paste(STUDY_DAYS, collapse = ", "), "."))
}
```

```{r sync-alternative}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(syncp)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_time_sync_pairs_2026.csv"))
} else {
  # The alternative explanation, checkable rather than argued away: the OSN
  # archive carries positions forward, which would bias the result in exactly
  # the direction measured.
  ok <- !is.na(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s) & !is.na(syncp$implied_dt_s)
  kable(data.frame(
    quantity = c("Median ADS-B position age", "Max ADS-B position age",
                 "corr(implied offset, ADS-B position age)"),
    value = c(paste0(p1(median(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok])), " s"),
              paste0(p1(max(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok])), " s"),
              p2(cor(syncp$implied_dt_s[ok], syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok])))),
    row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("", "Measured"),
    caption = paste("Could the offset be ADS-B's own staleness rather than",
                    "ADS-C's skew? The archive carries positions forward, so",
                    "the question has to be answered from the data."))
}
```

```{r sync-per-airframe}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(sync)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_time_sync_2026.csv"))
} else {
  pa <- sync[sync$icao24 != "ALL", ]
  pa <- pa[order(pa$median_implied_dt_s), ]
  kable(pa[, c("icao24", "n", "median_implied_dt_s", "std_implied_dt_s",
               "median_abs_cross_m")],
        row.names = FALSE, digits = 2,
        col.names = c("Airframe", "Pairs", "Median implied offset (s)",
                      "sigma (s)", "Median |cross| (m)"),
        caption = paste("Per airframe. The question this table decides: is the",
                        "skew a property of the feed, which one constant could",
                        "correct, or of the individual aircraft, which it",
                        "could not?"))
}
```

```{r sync-prose}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (is.null(sync) || is.null(syncp)) {
  cat(missing_note("the time-sync outputs"))
} else {
  a  <- sync[sync$icao24 == "ALL", ]
  pa <- sync[sync$icao24 != "ALL", ]
  ok <- !is.na(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s) & !is.na(syncp$implied_dt_s)
  ratio <- a$median_abs_along_m / max(a$median_abs_cross_m, 1e-9)
  v_cruise <- 240
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "Four things follow, in order.\n\n",
    "**It is timing, not position.** The along-track disagreement is %s m ",
    "against %s m across track, a ratio of %s. A position error is isotropic ",
    "and would land equally in both, so a ratio of that size cannot be one. ",
    "The two feeds agree about *where the track is* to within a few metres.\n\n",
    "**ADS-B carry-forward explains the tail, not the centre.** The OSN ",
    "archive carries positions forward, which biases this measurement in ",
    "exactly the direction observed, so the alternative has to be settled ",
    "from the data rather than argued away. ADS-B's own position age is %s s ",
    "at the median -- about %s m at cruise, far too little to account for a ",
    "%s m along-track displacement -- and it correlates with the implied ",
    "offset at only %s, so it is not driving the central tendency. But it ",
    "reaches **%s s** at the extreme, which is %s km at cruise, and that is ",
    "more than enough to produce the largest offsets in the per-airframe ",
    "table below. The honest division: the median is ADS-C skew, and the ",
    "tail is at least partly a stale reference. The prototype behind this ",
    "study saw a maximum age of 0.92 s and concluded carry-forward was ",
    "excluded outright; at %sx more pairs that conclusion does not survive ",
    "and is narrowed here.\n\n",
    "**It is one number per aircraft, not one number -- and a noisy one.** ",
    "Within-airframe standard deviations span %s-%s s, so some airframes are ",
    "stable and others are not; between airframes the median offset runs from ",
    "%s s to %s s. The spread *between* aircraft dwarfs anything a single ",
    "value could track, which is why ",
    "`AdscConfig.time_offset_seconds` ships at zero: a single constant would ",
    "be wrong for nearly every aircraft and would actively damage the ones ",
    "that are already synchronised. A per-airframe offset, estimated on ",
    "coverage-overlap data and applied where ADS-B is absent, is the real ",
    "fix; it needs a stability study across weeks before it could be ",
    "believed, and %s airframes over three days cannot support one. It is not ",
    "attempted here.\n\n",
    "**It matters less than the alternative.** At a cruise speed of about %d ",
    "m/s the median offset is roughly %s m. The alternative to having an ",
    "ADS-C sample at all is a straight line interpolated across a reception ",
    "hole of several hundred seconds, whose own error is tens of kilometres. ",
    "The skew is therefore a correction worth reporting and **not** a reason ",
    "to withhold the merge.\n\n"),
    p1(a$median_abs_along_m), p1(a$median_abs_cross_m), p1(ratio),
    p2(median(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok])),
    p1(median(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok]) * v_cruise),
    p1(a$median_abs_along_m),
    p2(cor(syncp$implied_dt_s[ok], syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok])),
    p1(max(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok])),
    p1(max(syncp$adsb_pos_age_s[ok]) * v_cruise / 1000),
    sprintf("%.0f", a$n / 46),
    p2(min(pa$std_implied_dt_s, na.rm = TRUE)),
    p2(max(pa$std_implied_dt_s, na.rm = TRUE)),
    signed(min(pa$median_implied_dt_s)), signed(max(pa$median_implied_dt_s)),
    nrow(pa), v_cruise,
    p1(abs(a$median_implied_dt_s) * v_cruise)))
}
```

One thing the skew does **not** reach: the derivative-spike filter.
`CleaningConfig.latlon_d1_max_deg_s` is 0.01 deg/s, about 1,100 m/s of apparent
ground speed, and a few hundred metres of displacement across a several-hundred
-second gap adds of the order of 0.001 deg/s. The filter is three orders of
magnitude away from seeing this error, so it neither corrects it nor is damaged
by it — which is also why no source guard was added there. Adding one would
have been machinery for a risk that is not present.

```{r holes-table}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(holes)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_holes_2026.csv"))
} else if (nrow(holes) == 0) {
  cat(paste("**No reception hole was closed.** Every surviving ADS-C sample",
            "sat within", HOLE_SECONDS, "s of an ADS-B sample on at least one",
            "side, so none of them added coverage the ADS-B feed did not",
            "already have. This is a result, not a missing table."))
} else {
  g <- pmin(holes$gap_before_s, holes$gap_after_s) / 60
  br <- c(0, 5, 10, 20, 60, Inf)
  tab <- table(cut(g, breaks = br, right = FALSE))
  kable(data.frame(band = names(tab), holes = as.integer(tab)),
        row.names = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Smaller side of the hole (minutes)", "ADS-C samples"),
        caption = paste(num(nrow(holes)), "ADS-C samples sat more than",
                        HOLE_SECONDS, "s from an ADS-B sample on **both**",
                        "sides. An infinite side means the sample extended the",
                        "track past its last ADS-B report, which is the",
                        "clearest case of added coverage."))
}
```

```{r gain-prose}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (is.null(gain)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_gain_2026.csv"))
} else {
  b <- gain[gain$arm == "base", ]
  m <- gain[gain$arm == "merged", ]
  d_tracks <- m$tracks - b$tracks
  new_only <- if ("tracks_all_adsc" %in% names(m)) m$tracks_all_adsc else NA
  # The count alone cannot be read. Three mechanisms move it and they do not
  # point the same way: bridging joins tracks (down), an airframe heard only
  # by ADS-C gains a track that had no baseline counterpart (up), and
  # splitting an existing track would also push it up (up, and harm). The
  # first reading of this study treated any rise as splitting, which was
  # wrong. `tracks_all_adsc` is what separates them.
  shared <- if (is.na(new_only)) NA else d_tracks - new_only
  verdict <- if (is.na(new_only)) {
    "cannot be attributed: `tracks_all_adsc` is not in this table"
  } else if (shared < 0) {
    sprintf(paste("decomposes into **%s new tracks** for airframes ADS-B never",
                  "heard in the window -- trajectories that had no baseline",
                  "counterpart at all -- against a **net %s** among the tracks",
                  "both arms share. The population they have in common got",
                  "*smaller*, which is what bridging does; the headline rise is",
                  "new coverage, not fragmentation"),
            num(new_only), num(shared))
  } else {
    sprintf(paste("decomposes into **%s new tracks** for airframes ADS-B never",
                  "heard against a net **%s** among shared tracks. A positive",
                  "figure there cannot come from bridging, which only joins:",
                  "it means tracks are being split, and nothing below should be",
                  "read as a coverage gain until that is explained"),
            num(new_only), num(shared))
  }
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "Reading those tables in order. **Something arrived**: %s ADS-C rows ",
    "survived cleaning -- %s%% of all rows in the merged arm, about one in ",
    "twelve thousand -- reaching %s of ",
    "%s tracks (%s%%). **The track count moved %s** -- %s against %s -- and ",
    "%s. **%s ADS-C samples closed a reception hole**, counted strictly: more ",
    "than %d s from an ADS-B sample on *both* sides, so a sample sitting ",
    "inside a dense stretch and seen as isolated from one direction does not ",
    "qualify. **The merge-neutrality guard** reads %s two-callsign tracks in ",
    "the merged arm against %s in the baseline -- a track holding two distinct ",
    "real callsigns is two flights fused into one, the way this change could ",
    "do real harm.\n\n",
    "One limit on that last pair of numbers, and on the net figure above: ",
    "both are aggregates. A net change of zero among shared tracks is ",
    "consistent with no change at all and equally with equal numbers of joins ",
    "and splits, so these rule out a dominant effect rather than an absent ",
    "one.\n\n"),
    num(m$rows_adsc), sprintf("%.4f", 100 * m$rows_adsc / m$rows),
    num(m$tracks_with_adsc), num(m$tracks),
    p1(100 * m$tracks_with_adsc / m$tracks),
    if (d_tracks > 0) sprintf("up %s", num(d_tracks)) else
      if (d_tracks < 0) sprintf("down %s", num(abs(d_tracks))) else "not at all",
    num(m$tracks), num(b$tracks), verdict,
    if (is.null(holes)) ABSENT else num(nrow(holes)), HOLE_SECONDS,
    num(m$tracks_with_two_callsigns), num(b$tracks_with_two_callsigns)))
}
```

# What it did to the flight events

```{r events-table}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(ev)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_events_2026.csv"))
} else {
  wide <- merge(
    ev[ev$arm == "base", c("milestone", "n_truth", "n_detected", "bias_s",
                           "mad_s")],
    ev[ev$arm == "merged", c("milestone", "n_detected", "bias_s", "mad_s")],
    by = "milestone", suffixes = c("_base", "_merged"))
  wide$delta_detected <- wide$n_detected_merged - wide$n_detected_base
  kable(wide, row.names = FALSE, digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "Both arms against APDF 202606, the twenty flight-events-v4 study",
    "aerodromes,", paste(STUDY_DAYS, collapse = ", "),
    ". `n_truth` is shared: one truth frame scores both arms, so a difference",
    "in `n_detected` is a difference in the pipeline and not in the",
    "reference."))
}
```

```{r events-by-airport}
#| echo: false
if (is.null(evap)) {
  cat(missing_note("adsc_events_by_airport_2026.csv"))
} else {
  # `gt_airport`, not `airport`: `score_by_airport` names the column after the
  # side it came from, because the aerodrome is the *reference's* opinion --
  # the detector's own runway/stand naming is scored separately. Merging on the
  # wrong key fails in R with "Error in fix.by()", which names neither column.
  key <- c("gt_airport", "milestone")
  b <- evap[evap$arm == "base", ]
  m <- evap[evap$arm == "merged", ]
  j <- merge(b, m, by = key, suffixes = c("_b", "_m"))
  j$delta <- j$n_detected_m - j$n_detected_b
  j$d_bias <- round(j$bias_s_m - j$bias_s_b, 3)
  moved <- j[j$delta != 0 | abs(j$d_bias) > 0.001,
             c("gt_airport", "milestone", "n_truth_b", "n_detected_b",
               "n_detected_m", "delta", "d_bias")]
  if (nrow(moved) == 0) {
    cat(sprintf(paste("**No (aerodrome, milestone) cell changed.** Across %d",
                      "cells -- %d aerodromes by %d scored milestones -- the",
                      "two arms detected the same movements with the same bias.",
                      "Read this beside the trajectory chapter: it is a null",
                      "result about *milestones*, not about coverage."),
                nrow(j), length(unique(j$gt_airport)),
                length(unique(j$milestone))))
  } else {
    kable(moved[order(-abs(moved$delta)), ], row.names = FALSE,
          col.names = c("Aerodrome", "Milestone", "Truth", "Base", "Merged",
                        "Delta", "Bias delta (s)"),
          caption = sprintf(paste("Every (aerodrome, milestone) cell where the",
                                  "arms differ -- %d of %d."),
                            nrow(moved), nrow(j)))
  }
}
```

```{r events-scope}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(ev)) {
  ms <- sort(unique(ev$milestone))
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "**Read what this table scores before reading what it says.** APDF can ",
    "score %d milestones -- %s -- and every one of them belongs to the A-CDM ",
    "and runway family. The families where ADS-C could physically contribute ",
    "(`first_seen`, `last_seen`, the flight-level crossings, and ADEP/ADES ",
    "through the flight list) are **not in the reference's vocabulary at ",
    "all**: APDF records aerodrome movements, not the moment an oceanic track ",
    "begins.\n\n",
    "So this chapter can confirm the predicted null and it **cannot detect ",
    "the gain**. That is a property of the reference, not a result. The ",
    "coverage ADS-C adds is measured in the previous chapter -- new tracks, ",
    "closed holes, track-hours -- and nothing APDF holds can corroborate or ",
    "contradict it. A reader who takes a flat table here as 'ADS-C adds ",
    "nothing' has drawn a conclusion the instrument cannot support.\n\n"),
    length(ms), paste0("`", paste(ms, collapse = "`, `"), "`")))
}
```

Whatever those tables show, one thing cannot be read out of them, and it is
worth stating before they are read at all: **the A-CDM and runway families
could not have moved.** ADS-C has no `on_ground` flag that is ever true, the
whole coverage box sees `r rng("in_box_below_10000ft")` of its rows a day below
ten thousand feet, and its cadence is several hundred seconds against detectors
that interpolate a runway-threshold crossing between adjacent samples. A flat
row for `ATOT`, `ALDT`, `AOBT` or `AIBT` is the expected outcome of adding this
feed, not a failure of the detector or of the measurement. The families where a
change is physically possible are the ones anchored at the edges of coverage —
`first_seen`, `last_seen`, the flight-level crossings, and ADEP/ADES through the
flight list for North Atlantic arrivals.

And for any event that *did* move, the move is not automatically an
improvement. Nothing in the pipeline prevents an event being interpolated
between an ADS-B and an ADS-C sample, so an event derived across that boundary
inherits the along-track displacement measured in the previous chapter. See the
limitations below.

# What this does not measure {#sec-limits}

Each of these is a measurement that was not made, not a result:

- **The reference cannot score the families ADS-C can reach.** APDF holds
  aerodrome movements: `ATOT`, `AOBT`, `AIBT`, `ALDT`. `first_seen`,
  `last_seen`, the flight-level crossings and ADEP/ADES are outside its
  vocabulary, so the milestone chapter confirms the predicted null on the
  A-CDM family and is *structurally incapable* of detecting a gain at the
  coverage edge. The trajectory chapter is the only evidence for that gain,
  and it has no independent reference to be checked against. Closing this
  would need a different reference -- Network Manager flight plans for the
  oceanic entry fixes, say -- not more days of APDF.
- **Only Europe.** Scoring is inside `EUROPE_BBOX`, and most of the in-box
  ADS-C rows sit in its Atlantic corner. The feed is global; a worldwide arm
  would see far more of it, and APDF could not score it.
- **Only June 2026, three days.** The flight-events-v4 period, chosen for
  comparability. ADS-C volumes in 2023–2024 are not scored, and the feed
  carried fewer columns then.
- **No shadow-window sweep.** −`r SHADOW_BEFORE_S`/+`r SHADOW_AFTER_S` s is a
  reasoned default, not a tuned one. A wider window drops more ADS-C; a
  narrower one admits near-duplicate positions. At the measured skew a
  symmetric window already catches every duplicate pair, so the asymmetry is
  what makes the time base explicit rather than a fix for a present failure.
- **No per-airframe time correction, and no stability study of the skew.** The
  time-synchronisation chapter measures the offset on three days and a few
  tens of airframes. Whether an airframe's offset is stable across weeks — the
  precondition for correcting it — is not measured here.
- **No IATA-to-ICAO callsign recovery.** The feed's `flight` field is discarded
  rather than mapped, so ADS-C contributes no callsign evidence to segmentation
  or to the flight list.
- **Nothing stops an event being interpolated across a source boundary.**
  `segment_id` splits at `r HOLE_SECONDS` s coverage holes and is read by **no
  detector** — `grep -rn segment_id src/opdi/pipeline/` finds it in two
  comments. An event derived between an ADS-B and an ADS-C sample therefore
  inherits the along-track displacement. This is pre-existing: the same
  detectors already interpolate across thirty-minute ADS-B holes. Making
  `segment_id` load-bearing would change published detector behaviour, so it is
  named here as a follow-up rather than changed on this branch.
- **The MLAT topic is untouched.** `readsb.aircraft.mlat.avro` is a second
  unused OpenSky source, denser than ADS-C — of the order of 374 objects a day
  — but starting only at 2026-05-18. It is multilateration, not ADS-C, and is
  out of scope.
- **No measurement of ADS-C positional accuracy.** `nic` and `rc` are constant
  zero in the feed, so the usual integrity containment bounds are unavailable.
  Nothing here establishes how accurate an ADS-C position is, only what
  including it changes — and the cross-track figure bounds the *disagreement*,
  which is not the same thing as an error.

# Reproducing this {#sec-reproduce}

```bash
# 1. The two arms. ~6 cluster-hours. Not regenerated by the entrypoint.
#    Day-major, not step-major: step 01 keeps a three-day sliding window and
#    drops what the window has passed, so ingesting every day before
#    segmenting any of them would hand day 05 a window two-thirds absent.
export PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv310/bin/python
unset PYSPARK_PYTHON OPDI_WAREHOUSE
for d in 2026-06-05 2026-06-06 2026-06-07; do
  .venv310/bin/python -u benchmarks/run_adsc_day.py --day $d --arm both
done

# 2. Every figure on this page.
.venv310/bin/python -u benchmarks/regenerate_adsc_v1.py

# 3. This page.
cd ../opdi-portal/papers && quarto render adsc-fusion-v1/index.qmd
```

# Provenance {#sec-provenance}

```{r provenance}
#| echo: false
mf <- file.path("data", "_manifest.json")
if (!file.exists(mf)) {
  cat(paste("**No manifest.** Every figure on this page is unverified:",
            "nothing records which script, arguments or commit produced it."))
} else {
  j <- jsonlite::fromJSON(mf, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(j), function(k) data.frame(
    output = k,
    script = j[[k]]$script %||% "",
    sha = j[[k]]$git_sha %||% "",
    dirty = isTRUE(j[[k]]$git_dirty),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  kable(rows, row.names = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Output", "Script", "Commit", "Dirty tree"),
        caption = paste("Each staged output, and the command that produced",
                        "it. A `dirty` row was produced from uncommitted",
                        "code: the number is real and cannot be reproduced",
                        "from a commit."))
}
```

```{r provenance-missing}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
expected <- c("adsc_census.csv", "adsc_gain_2026.csv", "adsc_holes_2026.csv",
              "adsc_time_sync_2026.csv", "adsc_time_sync_pairs_2026.csv",
              "adsc_events_2026.csv", "adsc_events_by_airport_2026.csv")
absent <- expected[!file.exists(file.path("data", expected))]
if (length(absent)) {
  cat(paste0("**Not staged:** `", paste(absent, collapse = "`, `"), "`. ",
             "The chapters above say so in place; this list is the index. ",
             "A draft with visible holes is honest; a draft with numbers of ",
             "unknown origin is not."))
} else {
  cat("All seven expected outputs are staged.")
}
```
